weekly: Introduction to Weekly Schedule, Course Content and Requirements. The framework of syllabus is based on concept development in addition to idea generation, fundamental principles of graphic design, visual thinking, the execution of digital and analog techniques and color theory in particular through lectures, demonstrations, extensive studio classwork, critique and feedback sessions.

Lecture: Expressing yourself in Drawing. Creative Process Sketchbook and Project 01: Page Redesign. The sketchbook is going to be a record of the student’s effort and dedication throughout the semester. The preparatory drawings and artworks which are regularly created by students each week, particularly along with research, experiments, thumbnails, written assessments and ideas, will make up the content of sketchbook.

Lectures: Design Process, The Principles of Design. These lectures will be the key considerations for the design process in terms of composing a successful graphic design project throughout the fall and spring semesters. The case studies which will be conducted in related practices are: Define – analyzing the source of problem, Research – collecting background information, Ideate – creating potential solutions, Prototype – resolving solutions, Select – making choices, Implementation– creating the visual medium, Learn - obtaining feedback. Work in Progress: Project 01: Page Redesign.

Lectures: Idea Generation, Creative Ideas. Project 02: Pictograms. Demonstrations such as Spider Diagrams, Mind Mapping, Brainstorming, Sketching will be undertaken to advance the student's experience in notion and idea generation. The topics providing key strategies, methods for generating ideas are composed of wide range of disciplines to produce innovative graphic design solutions.
Lecture: Semiotics in Graphic Design. The Study of Signs and Symbols as Elements of Communicative Behaviour. Icon, Index and Symbol. Work in Progress: Project 02: Pictograms.
Project 03: Alphabet.
Work in Progress: Project 03: Alphabet.

Lecture: Visual Thinking. Project 04: Typo Portrait. The lecture and assignment are going to examine the importance of harmony between image, typography, color and visual diversity of combinations to fortify the effectiveness of message.
Work in Progress: Project 04: Typo Portrait.

Lecture: Color Theory. Assignment 05 - Color Studies. The lecture and assignment consist of the fundamentals of color perception, color interaction and unity in addition to color meanings, color systems in Art and Design History and practising on digital and print mediums.
Work in Progress: Project 05: Color Studies.

weekly: Course Introduction & Visual Thinking. Overview of course objectives, tools, expectations. Lecture: What is Illustration? (functions, history, contemporary fields). Traditional Tools: Graphite pencils (2H, HB, 2B, 4B, 6B), Mechanical pencil (0.3 / 0.5mm), Erasers, Sharpener. Black waterproof ink, Watercolors (basic 12-color set, tubes), Water brush or round watercolor brushes (sizes 2, 6, 10), Sketchbook (A4 or A3, 120–160 gsm for dry media), Watercolor paper (200–300 gsm, cold press, if using wet media), Tracing paper (for transferring sketches). Digital Tools: Computer or tablet (laptop + drawing tablet, or iPad with Apple Pencil, or Wacom/XP-Pen), Drawing software (Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, Procreate). Portfolio folder (A3) for finished works.

Drawing Foundations. Focus: line, mark-making & texture, form, proportion, gesture drawing. Explore expressive line qualities. Techniques: cross-hatching, stippling, continuous line. Lecture: Expressing yourself in Drawing. Assignment: Abstract composition using only line/texture. The perception of beauty and ugliness.

Value & Light. Focus: Shading, contrast, light sources, atmosphere. Tonal studies. Illustration with dramatic lighting. Shading techniques (graphite, ink wash). Lecture: Theory of imagery. Assignment: Illustration with dramatic lighting.

Composition & Visual Storytelling. Focus: Composition Principles, rule of thirds, balance, focal point, negative space, storytelling through images. Analyzing classic illustrations. Lecture: The Principle of Design. Assignment: Re-illustrate a short fable in 3 panels.
Color Theory for Illustration. Focus: Color psychology, palettes, harmony, mood. Lecture: Colour. Assignment: Create an illustration using a limited color palette.
Medium Exploration I (Traditional). Focus: Experimentation with watercolor, colored pencil, or markers. Assignment: Same subject illustrated in two different traditional mediums.
Medium Exploration II (Digital). Focus: Basics of digital illustration software (Photoshop, Procreate, Illustrator). Activity: Digital Collage.

Character Design. Focus: Personality through shapes, silhouettes, expressions, poses. Goal: Learn shape language and how form communicates personality. Lecture: How to have creative ideas. Assignment: Design a unique character with 3 expressions and 3 poses.
Illustration for Print & Editorial. Focus: Spot illustrations, magazine covers, visual metaphors. Lecture: Visual Metaphor. Assignment: Create an editorial illustration for an article headline.
Narrative & Sequential Art. Focus: Storyboarding, comics, visual pacing. Assignment: 1–2 page short comic strip or storyboard sequence. Illustrate Your Own Story.

Developing a Personal Style. Focus: Exploration of influences, experimenting with techniques, building consistency. Lecture: POV. Assignment: Create a set of 3 related illustrations in your emerging style.

Final Creative Personal Projects. Focus: Planning, sketches, feedback, revisions. Activity: Work on a self-directed final illustration project (editorial piece, book cover, children’s book spread, or personal narrative). Lecture: What is semiotics and why we use them.
Final Hybrid Illustration Experiment. Combine traditional and digital techniques. Explore mixed media approaches.

Presentation. Write a short reflective statement (150-200 words) discussing your process, choices, and what you learned. Present your work to the class and participate in critique. Process Work: Sketches, color studies, and drafts (can be presented digitally or in a sketchbook).
